name: Synth-built pitch riser: 2-octave bend ramp with reset points, smeared by a resonant diffusion filter and reverb
goal: Build a synth-only riser that does not sour the key: one saw swept by a full-clip pitch-bend ramp from -1 to +1 octave (with reset points so mid-clip playback starts clean), then smeared by a low-set, high-resonance phase-smearing (comb/allpass-diffusion style) filter with a slight slow LFO and a reverb, so the listener hears a rising swarm rather than a clearly out-of-key moving pitch.

source.title: Serum Tutorial - How To Make Risers

prerequisites: Synth with pitch-bend range, an LFO and a resonant filter with a smear/diffusion-like type (or a short feedback comb/allpass network)

inputs.name: riser_length
inputs.description: Length of the build section the riser spans

outputs.name: smeared_riser
outputs.description: Two-octave rising tone with blurred pitch

steps.action: Start with a single oscillator on a saw wave (choose the tone you want); turn effects off while setting up.
Set the pitch-bend range to 12 semitones so a full bend travels from -1 octave to +1 octave (two octaves total) - the bend range defines the distance the riser travels.

Automate pitch bend as one ramp across the entire clip, starting exactly at the bottom (-1 oct) and ending exactly at the top (+1 oct). Add small reset points at the clip start and end that return bend to 0, so playback started partway through does not begin with a mangled/latched pitch.
steps.expect: Clean rise every time the clip restarts

steps.action: Recognise the problem: a constantly moving pitch only lands on an in-key note for a split second, so if the pitch is clearly discernible it makes the track sound sour - so smear it.

Insert a phase-smearing resonant filter (source: a 'reverb'-type filter; portable alias: short comb/allpass diffusion filter). Set cutoff LOW with HIGH resonance - set high it affects too little of the sound; low with high resonance it blurs where the pitch was into where it is.
Add an LFO for very slight, slow movement of that filter: with no movement it does not smudge, with too much movement the effect is lost.
steps.expect: Moving smear that hides discrete pitch

steps.action: Add reverb afterwards to smear further (its micro-delays carry the pitch just passed into the current pitch).
steps.expect: 'Swarm of bees rising' character, less menacing in the mix

steps.action: Optional finishing (not vital to the sound): sidechain compression, basic EQ, auto-pan pumping.

verification: Pitch at clip start and end equals exactly -1 and +1 octave; restarting mid-clip gives no latched pitch
A/B filter cutoff high vs low: low+resonant smears noticeably more
With smear filter + reverb the riser's pitch is hard to name, but the upward motion is clear
constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there. Numbers quoted are the presenter's approximate values, in the source tool's own units.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only - map brand UI (Serum/Bitwig/Ableton/Logic/Cubase/Zebra/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for a Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid (Polyrhythm Studio); never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
